source_text:
Ὑπακούσωμεν οὖν τῷ παναγίῳ καὶ ἐνδόξῳ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ φυγόντες τὰς προειρημένας διὰ τῆς σοφίας τοῖς ἀπειθοῦσιν ἀπειλάς, ἵνα κατασκηνώσωμεν πεποιθότες ἐπὶ τὸ ὁσιώτατον τῆς μεγαλωσύνης αὐτοῦ ὄνομα.
δέξασθε τὴν συμβουλὴν ἡμῶν, καὶ ἔσται ἀμεταμέλητα ὑμῖν. ζῇ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς καὶ ζῇ ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἥ τε πίστις καὶ ἡ ἐλπὶς τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν, ὅτι ὁ ποιήσας ἐν ταπεινοφροσύνῃ μετ’ ἐκτενοῦς ἐπιεικείας ἀμεταμελήτως τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ δεδομένα δικαιώματα καὶ προστάγματα, οὗτος ἐντεταγμένος καὶ ἐλλόγιμος ἔσται εἰς τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν σωζομένων διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δἰ οὖ ἐστὶν αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
thought_title: Obedience to God's holy name and the reward of the saved
orientation: The Roman church is concluding its appeal to the Corinthians, urging them to obey God and accept the letter's counsel so that they may be counted among the saved.
pass_a_gloss: Let us therefore obey his all-holy and glorious name, having fled the threats spoken beforehand through wisdom to those who disobey, in order that we may dwell trusting in the most holy name of his majesty. Accept our counsel, and it will be without regret for you. For the God lives and the Lord Jesus Christ lives and the Holy Spirit, and the faith and the hope of the elect, that the one who has done in humility with earnest gentleness without regret the righteous acts and commandments given by God, this one will be enrolled and counted among the number of those being saved through Jesus Christ, through whom is to him the glory unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: The hortatory subjunctive includes the authors with the Corinthians in the appeal; 'obey' keeps the force of hearing under authority.
The aorist participle expresses prior escape from the threats; 'fled' preserves the urgency of the image.
The adjective is used twice in this section; rendering it consistently as 'without regret' preserves the wordplay and the sense of no later remorse.
Both terms evoke a register or list; 'enrolled and counted' keeps the administrative metaphor of being inscribed among the saved.
The present participle conveys an ongoing process of salvation, not a completed state.

choices.english: unto the ages of the ages
choices.why: The literal rendering preserves the liturgical formula's repetitive structure.

pass_b_english: Let us obey His all-holy and glorious name, then, and flee from the threats that Wisdom spoke beforehand against the disobedient. Then we may dwell in trust upon the most holy name of His majesty.

Accept our counsel, and you will have no regret. For as God lives, and as the Lord Jesus Christ lives, and as the Holy Spirit lives, and as the faith and hope of the elect live, so surely the one who has done the righteous acts and commandments given by God, in humility with earnest gentleness, without regret, will be enrolled and counted among the number of those being saved through Jesus Christ. Through Him is the glory to God unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

polish.changed: Clarified the oath formula by repeating 'lives' for each divine witness, named God as the recipient of glory, and smoothed the sentence flow while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.why: Reader may not recognize these all refer to the same group.

polish.changed: Clarified the long oath sentence by keeping the 'as...so surely' structure explicit, so readers can follow the condition and its result without losing the original claims.

last_rejected.why: Greek 'ἐντεγμένος' means 'enrolled, assigned, appointed'; 'ἐλλόγιμος' means 'reckoned, counted, esteemed'. English 'enrolled and counted' captures both. But 'ἔσται' is future indicative 'will be', not a command. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: ἔσται is correctly rendered as future 'will be'; ἐντεταγμένος and ἐλλόγιμος are accurately translated as 'enrolled and counted'.

last_rejected.why: Wait—'ἐλλόγιμος' means 'reckoned, counted, held in account'. The English adds 'counted' which is interpretation of 'ἐλλόγιμος'. But 'ἐλλόγιμος' itself means 'accountable, reckoned'—the English 'counted among' is a rendering. Is this addition? The Greek has two predicates: 'enrolled and reckoned'. English 'enrolled and counted' reflects both. Not an addition.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐλλόγιμος means 'reckoned, counted'; English 'counted' renders it, not an addition. Both Greek predicates are represented.

last_rejected.why: Greek 'ἀμεταμελήτως' means 'irrevocably, without changing one's mind, unrepentingly'—adverb modifying how the person does the righteous acts. English 'without regret' goes with the person ('you will have no regret' earlier is 'ἀμεταμέλητα'). Here 'without regret' is slightly off; better 'unhesitatingly' or 'without turning back'. But 'without regret' in the sense of 'without remorse or second thoughts' is within range.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀμεταμελήτως means 'without regret/repentance'; 'without regret' is within normal range, not a mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: The 'ὅτι' after the oath formula introduces the content of what is sworn: 'that the one who...' English 'so surely' captures the asseverative force. The oath is 'as God lives... so [surely]...' This is a legitimate literary rendering of the Hebrew/Greek oath formula.
last_rejected.ruling: ὅτι in oath formula introduces sworn content; 'so surely' captures asseverative force of the Greek oath construction.

last_rejected.why: Greek 'ὁ ποιήσας' is aorist participle 'the one who has done'. English correct. But the construction is 'the one who has done... will be enrolled'. This is a condition: whoever does X will be Y. English captures this.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ ποιήσας is aorist participle 'the one who has done'; English is correct and captures the conditional sense.

last_rejected.quote: unto the ages of the ages
last_rejected.why: English has 'unto the ages of the ages'. This is complete. No omission.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων is fully rendered as 'unto the ages of the ages'; no omission exists.

last_rejected.quote: So surely the one who has done the righteous acts and commandments
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ ποιήσας ἐν ταπεινοφροσύνῃ μετ’ ἐκτενοῦς ἐπιεικείας ἀμεταμελήτως τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ δεδομένα δικαιώματα καὶ προστάγματα
last_rejected.why: The English reads as though the acts themselves are righteous and done by the person. The source says he who performs the ordinances and commandments given by God. Also 'so surely' misplaces the oath's force.
last_rejected.fix: the one who has carried out, in humility with earnest gentleness and without regret, the ordinances and commandments given by God
last_rejected.ruling: δικαιώματα covers righteous deeds and ordinances; δεδομένα is kept. ‘so surely’ correctly marks the ζῇ…ὅτι oath on ἔσται.
